ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AE \perp BD$ at point $E$, and $\angle DAE = 2\angle BAE$, what is the measure of $\angle EAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
it follows that OA=OC=OB=OD, and $\angle$BAD=$90^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle$ABO=$\angle$BAO,\\
given that $\angle$DAE=2$\angle$BAE, and $\angle$DAE+$\angle$BAE=$90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle$BAE=$30^\circ$,\\
given that AE$\perp$BD, that is $\angle$AEB=$90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle$ABO=$60^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle$BAO=$60^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle$EAC=$\angle$BAO−$\angle$BAE=$60^\circ−30^\circ=\boxed{30^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: ABCD is drawn as a rectangle with A top-left, B bottom-left, C bottom-right, D top-right; diagonals AC and BD are drawn, E lies on BD, and AE is drawn to E. Let x = ∠BAE. From the text and rectangle angle ∠BAD = 90°, AE splits ∠BAD into ∠BAE = x and ∠DAE = 2x, so 3x = 90° and x = 30°. Since AE ⟂ BD at E, triangle ABE is right at E; because E is on BD, ∠ABE is the angle between AB and BD. Then ∠ABE = 180° - 90° - 30° = 60°. In a rectangle, the two diagonals make equal acute angles with corresponding sides; equivalently, if BD makes 60° with vertical AB, then AC also makes 60° with vertical AB on the other side from A toward C. Reasoning: Let ∠BAE = x. Because ABCD is a rectangle, ∠BAD = 90°. AE divides ∠BAD into ∠BAE and ∠DAE, and the problem statement gives ∠DAE = 2∠BAE, so x + 2x = 90°, obtaining x = 30°, that is, ∠BAE = 30°. Also because AE ⟂ BD at E, triangle ABE is right-angled at E, ∠AEB = 90°. Therefore ∠ABE = 180° - 90° - 30° = 60°. Since E is on BD, ∠ABE is the angle between AB and diagonal BD. In a rectangle, the acute angles formed by the two diagonals with the corresponding sides are equal, so the angle ∠BAC formed by AC and AB is also 60°. From the figure, AE is located between AB and AC, therefore ∠EAC = ∠BAC - ∠BAE = 60° - 30° = 30°.
